comparisons.peer_summary: AMD has an approved stock repurchase program authorizing up to $12 billion in repurchases, with $4.7 billion available as of December 28, 2024, which may be suspended or discontinued at any time and could affect cash reserves and stock volatility.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose share repurchase programs with specific authorization amounts but explicitly state that these authorizations do not obligate the companies to purchase any specific amount of stock. Micron reported $300 million in repurchases for 2024 under a $10 billion authorization, whereas AMD reported $4.7 billion remaining available for future repurchases out of a $12 billion total authorization. Both companies highlight the discretion and flexibility in execution, noting that repurchases are subject to fluctuation based on cash needs and priorities, and neither guarantees that the authorization will enhance shareholder value or be fully consummated.

sentences.text: The amount, frequency, and execution of our share repurchases pursuant to our share repurchase authorization may fluctuate based on our operating results, cash flows, and priorities for the use of cash for other purposes.
Our expenditures for these share repurchases were $300 million in 2024, $425 million in 2023, $2.43 billion in 2022, $1.20 billion in 2021, $176 million in 2020, and $2.66 billion in 2019.
Although our Board of Directors has authorized share repurchases of up to $10 billion of our outstanding common stock, the authorization does not obligate us to repurchase any common stock.
We have an approved stock repurchase program that authorizes repurchases of up to $12 billion of our common stock (Repurchase Program).
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under the Repurchase Program.
The Repurchase Program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

comparisons.peer_topic: Debt Obligations and Capital Return Restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces risks related to its significant debt obligations ($51.0 billion in senior unsecured notes as of Dec 28, 2024) and cyclical industry nature, which pose risks to its financial condition, including potential credit rating downgrades that have already occurred in 2024. Additionally, Intel has ceased stock repurchases and suspended its quarterly dividend in Q4 2024, with additional restrictions under the CHIPS Act agreement creating uncertainty regarding future dividend payments or share repurchases.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose their share repurchase programs with explicit disclaimers that they are not obligated to repurchase any stock. While Micron actively spent $300 million in 2024 under its authorization, Intel discloses that it is 'not obligated to make repurchases' and provides no assurance on timing or execution, reflecting a divergent operational reality despite similar boilerplate language regarding the non-obligatory nature of the programs.
